title: World-C skim-de-buffering owner footgun: routinely running skimSurplus strips the protective vault-rate over-collateralization buffer for zero upside, removing the depeg cushion ahead of a possible sUSDe discount
derivedFrom: M-01-run12 (collapsed to invalid). This is the honest QA-level residual the collapse PoC (World-C) and the independent adversarial validator flagged after the Medium claim resolved into acknowledged M-02.
description: skimSurplus harvests the vault-rate surplus, which includes the deposit-time slippage-haircut over-collateralization buffer (held·p − D) that absorbs any sUSDe AMM discount. Running skimSurplus routinely (e.g. as a scheduled keeper/operator hygiene action) strips this buffer for no protocol upside — the surplus is owner/client-directed yield that is not at risk if left in place — while removing the cushion ahead of a possible sUSDe depeg. Crucially the realized loss does NOT reach depositors on any protocol withdrawal path: under a beyond-tolerance discount (World-C) every protocol withdrawal path reverts rather than realizing a shortfall. The loss materializes only via the owner's own emergencyWithdraw + OTC force-sale of the restricted shares at the discounted rate, so it is Law-3 owner-bounded, not a depositor-reachable Medium.
impact: No depositor-reachable asset or availability impact: under a beyond-tolerance discount all protocol withdrawal paths revert rather than realize the shortfall (confirmed by the collapse PoC's World-C test and the adversarial validator). The realized loss is reachable only through the owner's own emergencyWithdraw + OTC force-sale — an owner-bounded operational hazard, not a depositor Medium.
likelihood: Operational owner/keeper footgun (Law-3 in-scope as a NON-OBVIOUS hazard): an operator routinely skimming for surplus hygiene would not expect to be eroding the protocol's depeg cushion for zero upside; a competent non-malicious owner would be surprised by the consequence.
assumptions: Owner/keeper runs skimSurplus routinely while a protective buffer exists; a sustained sUSDe AMM discount later materializes; the owner then realizes the loss via emergencyWithdraw + OTC sale.
externalRequirements: A sustained sUSDe NAV/AMM discount AND an owner emergencyWithdraw + OTC force-sale to actually realize the loss. Same vault-rate-vs-AMM-rate root cause as acknowledged M-02; the depositor-reaching escalation was disproved by the M-01-run12 PoC collapse.
justification: Demoted from the collapsed M-01-run12 Medium. The collapse PoC (World-C) and the independent adversarial validator confirm the only path past M-02's slippageBps × tradeSize bound is the owner's own escape hatch, so this is NOT a depositor Medium. safeConfigGuidance: Do not run skimSurplus as a routine/scheduled hygiene action. Skim only against a realized, durable surplus, and retain a protocol-favoring buffer at skim time (recommendation (b) from M-01-run12) so de-buffering cannot strip the discount cushion ahead of a depeg. Treat emergencyWithdraw + OTC sale of restricted shares under a live discount as the genuine loss locus and gate it accordingly.
recommendation: Either retain a protocol-favoring buffer at skim time so the de-buffering cannot strip the discount cushion, or document operationally that skimSurplus should not be run routinely while a depeg risk exists. No on-chain mitigation is strictly owed beyond the M-02 acknowledgement; this is surfaced so the operational hazard is not lost.
